passages.p1:
Hi Mia,

Thanks for inviting me to your [[1]] party on Saturday. I'd love to come, but I need to [[2]] my cousin at the airport. Her flight was delayed, so I'm not sure when we'll get back. Could you [[3]] me the address by text? If I arrive late, please don't [[4]] for me before eating. I can [[5]] a sandwich on the way. I hope the weather stays [[6]], since the garden gets muddy after rain.

Best, Sam
passages.p2: Put the sentences in the correct order to make a story. The first one is done for you.
passages.p3:
Most great ranges are not primordial excrescences but transient expressions of lithospheric instability. Where an oceanic plate descends beneath a continental margin, magma generation, crustal compression and accretion of sediments progressively thicken the overriding landmass. Elsewhere, the collision of two buoyant continents produces intense folding and faulting because neither slab readily sinks. Isostatic adjustment then raises the thickened crust, while rivers, frost and mass wasting simultaneously dismantle it. Consequently, spectacular relief records a prolonged contest between tectonic uplift and denudation, rather than a single catastrophic event.

Although their surface area is modest, upland regions often contain an exceptional concentration of endemic organisms. Sharp shifts in altitude create adjacent thermal zones, moisture regimes and soil types over very short distances, permitting ecological specialisation. Deep valleys and isolated ridges can also prevent interbreeding, so populations diverge genetically and become restricted to one locality. This spatial complexity shelters orchids, amphibians, insects and conifers that may occur nowhere else. Yet such richness is precarious: road building, forest clearance and altered fire patterns fragment already limited habitats, making high-elevation conservation disproportionately consequential.

Snowfields, seasonal snowpack, glaciers and high-altitude wetlands intercept precipitation and release it gradually, thereby regulating the timing of river discharge. For this reason, densely populated lowlands may depend on headwaters situated hundreds of kilometres away. The stored water irrigates crops, replenishes aquifers, supports hydropower and moderates dry-season scarcity. Vegetation and soils on slopes further influence filtration and sediment loads, so degradation upstream can compromise both quantity and quality downstream. Describing these regions merely as scenic overlooks therefore obscures their hydrological function within continental economies.

Residents of steep, isolated districts have developed social arrangements that cannot be reduced to picturesque tradition. Terraced cultivation, transhumant herding, communal irrigation and reciprocal labour are practical responses to thin soils, abrupt weather and difficult transport. Linguistic minorities and distinctive ceremonial calendars frequently persist because valleys historically limited outside contact. However, outmigration, digital connectivity and tourism are reconfiguring these societies; younger inhabitants may combine wage employment with ancestral land-use practices. Effective policy must consequently recognise local expertise rather than treating upland people as passive custodians of an immutable past.

Rising air temperatures have shifted the mass balance of many glaciers: annual melting increasingly exceeds accumulation from snowfall. As ice tongues thin and retreat, they initially may enlarge meltwater flows, but this temporary surplus can be followed by severe reductions once ice reserves are depleted. Newly exposed slopes also destabilise, raising the likelihood of rockfalls and sudden floods from moraine-dammed lakes. The repercussions extend beyond alpine scenery, since communities and irrigation systems reliant on predictable seasonal runoff face mounting uncertainty. Monitoring programmes thus treat glacier loss as a socioeconomic as well as a cryospheric emergency.

Across numerous civilisations, elevated summits have been imagined not simply as physical prominences but as points of communication with gods, ancestors or cosmic forces. Pilgrims undertake arduous approaches to particular peaks, while oral narratives locate creation, revelation or heroic encounters on their slopes. Such associations can impose taboos on hunting, cutting trees or entering certain zones, inadvertently protecting habitats. They can also generate disputes when state agencies, climbers or developers overlook sacred restrictions. To interpret these landscapes exclusively through geology is therefore to ignore the symbolic authority that shapes human conduct around them.

Technical ascents, long-distance trekking, skiing and guided expeditions now generate substantial income in many highland economies. Visitors may finance lodges, portering, equipment hire and conservation fees, broadening livelihoods where agriculture is constrained. Nonetheless, the sector is marked by asymmetrical risk: local guides often confront hazardous conditions for relatively modest remuneration, while waste, trail erosion and overcrowding burden fragile terrain. Commercial operators must therefore manage carrying capacity, safety standards and benefit distribution rather than equating increased visitor numbers with development. Adventure travel can be valuable, but only when its environmental and social costs are not externalised.

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If you _____ to need help, just ask the teacher.
questions.explanation:
If' mang nghĩa 'mỗi khi/nếu' nên dùng hiện tại đơn 'happen', không dùng 'would' trong mệnh đề if.
[TD]Dịch: Nếu bạn tình cờ cần giúp đỡ, cứ hỏi cô giáo.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He _____ be rich, but he is not very kind to people.
questions.explanation:
May' diễn tả sự nhượng bộ ('có thể đúng là... nhưng...').
[TD]Dịch: Anh ta có thể giàu, nhưng anh ta không tử tế với mọi người lắm.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If only he _____ smoking when the doctor told him, he would be healthy now.
questions.explanation:
If only' + quá khứ hoàn thành 'had given up' diễn tả tiếc nuối về quá khứ, kéo theo kết quả hiện tại.
[TD]Dịch: Giá mà anh ấy đã bỏ thuốc khi bác sĩ khuyên, thì bây giờ anh ấy đã khỏe mạnh.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She _____ her assistant of leaking the confidential merger details to a rival firm.
questions.explanation:
Cấu trúc 'accuse sb of + V-ing' (buộc tội ai làm gì) đúng giới từ, khác 'blame sb for'.
[TD]Dịch: Cô ấy buộc tội trợ lý của mình đã làm rò rỉ chi tiết thương vụ sáp nhập mật cho một công ty đối thủ.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

It is reported that the old house _____ to a new owner.
questions.explanation:
Bị động hoàn thành 'has been sold' diễn tả việc ngôi nhà đã được bán.
[TD]Dịch: Có tin rằng ngôi nhà cũ đã được bán cho chủ mới.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

That _____ Tom at the door. He said he would come tonight.
questions.explanation:
Will be' diễn tả sự suy đoán chắc chắn về hiện tại (hẳn là).
[TD]Dịch: Đó hẳn là Tom ở ngoài cửa. Anh ấy nói sẽ đến tối nay.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He made the decision without asking anyone, and his team _____ it ever since.
questions.explanation:
Hiện tại hoàn thành 'have regretted' với 'ever since' diễn tả sự tiếc nuối kéo dài từ quá khứ đến nay.
[TD]Dịch: Anh ấy đã quyết định mà không hỏi ai, và đội của anh hối tiếc kể từ đó đến giờ.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

In the past, people _____ to bow when they met someone important.
questions.explanation:
Used to' diễn tả phong tục/thói quen từng tồn tại trong quá khứ nay đã mất.
[TD]Dịch: Ngày xưa, mọi người thường cúi chào khi gặp người quan trọng.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He arrived _____ for the meeting because his flight had been delayed for hours.
questions.explanation:
Cần tính từ/trạng từ 'late' (muộn); 'lately' nghĩa 'gần đây' nên không hợp ngữ cảnh.
[TD]Dịch: Anh ấy đến muộn cuộc họp vì chuyến bay đã bị hoãn nhiều giờ.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ majority of the students passed the test.
questions.explanation:
The majority of' dùng mạo từ xác định 'the' khi nói về đa số một nhóm cụ thể.
[TD]Dịch: Đa số học sinh đã đỗ bài kiểm tra.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You _____ told me you don't eat meat before I cooked dinner!
questions.explanation:
Might have + V3' diễn tả lời trách móc về việc lẽ ra nên làm.
[TD]Dịch: Lẽ ra bạn nên nói cho tôi biết bạn không ăn thịt trước khi tôi nấu bữa tối chứ![/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

We would have been late _____ the taxi driver's fast driving.
questions.explanation:
But for' nghĩa là 'nếu không có', dẫn danh từ để chỉ nguyên nhân giả định.
[TD]Dịch: Chúng tôi đã bị muộn nếu không nhờ tài xế taxi lái nhanh.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If you _____ me, I think this movie is not very good.
questions.explanation:
Câu điều kiện thực diễn tả ý kiến hiện tại, dùng hiện tại đơn 'ask' trong mệnh đề if.
[TD]Dịch: Nếu bạn hỏi tôi, tôi nghĩ bộ phim này không hay lắm.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You can borrow my flat in Vienna _____ you water the plants and feed the cat.
questions.explanation:
As long as' nêu điều kiện (miễn là), phù hợp ngữ cảnh cho phép có kèm điều kiện.
[TD]Dịch: Bạn có thể mượn căn hộ của tôi ở Vienna miễn là bạn tưới cây và cho mèo ăn.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ you happen to see Lan at school, please give her this book.
questions.explanation:
If + happen to' diễn tả tình huống tình cờ; dùng 'If' cho điều kiện thông thường.
[TD]Dịch: Nếu bạn tình cờ gặp Lan ở trường, hãy đưa cho cô ấy cuốn sách này.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ the bridge been built stronger, it wouldn't be damaged now.
questions.explanation:
Đảo ngữ câu điều kiện: 'Had + chủ ngữ + V3' thay cho 'If... had' diễn tả giả định trái với quá khứ.
[TD]Dịch: Giá như cây cầu được xây chắc hơn, thì bây giờ nó đã không bị hỏng.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Direct: 'You shouldn't have spent so much money on that toy.' Reported: Mom told me I _____ so much money on that toy.
questions.explanation:
Shouldn't have + V3' đã ở quá khứ nên giữ nguyên khi tường thuật.
[TD]Dịch: Mẹ nói lẽ ra tôi không nên tiêu nhiều tiền vào món đồ chơi đó.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I found a girl _____ voice is really beautiful.
questions.explanation:
Whose' là đại từ quan hệ chỉ sở hữu, thay cho 'the girl's voice'.
[TD]Dịch: Tôi tìm thấy một cô gái mà giọng hát rất hay.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I will lend you my bike _____ that you return it by Friday.
questions.explanation:
On condition (that)' nêu điều kiện ràng buộc (với điều kiện là).
[TD]Dịch: Tôi sẽ cho bạn mượn xe đạp với điều kiện bạn trả lại trước thứ Sáu.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

My friend _____ going to the new restaurant for dinner.
questions.explanation:
Động từ 'suggest' đi với V-ing (không dùng 'suggest sb to do').
[TD]Dịch: Bạn tôi đề nghị đi ăn tối ở nhà hàng mới.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ have a quick coffee somewhere before catching the late train?
questions.explanation:
Shall we...?' dùng để đưa ra lời đề nghị, rủ rê cùng làm gì đó.
[TD]Dịch: Chúng ta đi uống cà phê nhanh đâu đó trước khi bắt chuyến tàu muộn nhé?[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You look tired!' 'Yes, I _____ for the test since this morning.'
questions.explanation:
Hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn 'have been studying' diễn tả hành động kéo dài từ 'since this morning' đến hiện tại.
[TD]Dịch: 'Trông cậu mệt quá!' 'Ừ, tớ đã ôn thi từ sáng đến giờ.'[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He was writing his essay when the lights went off, and he realized he _____ to save it.
questions.explanation:
Quá khứ hoàn thành 'had forgotten' diễn tả việc quên xảy ra trước thời điểm mất điện.
[TD]Dịch: Anh ấy đang viết bài luận thì đèn tắt, và anh nhận ra mình đã quên lưu bài.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The plan has been _____ for several weeks.
questions.explanation:
Cụm danh từ 'under consideration' (đang được xem xét) tránh thể bị động.
[TD]Dịch: Kế hoạch đã được xem xét trong vài tuần.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The proposal was _____ rejected by the entire board without further discussion.
questions.explanation:
Trạng từ 'flatly' (thẳng thừng) đi với 'rejected'; 'very/rather' không bổ nghĩa cho động từ kiểu này.
[TD]Dịch: Đề xuất bị cả hội đồng thẳng thừng bác bỏ mà không bàn bạc thêm.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

The first meal you eat in the morning
questions.explanation:
breakfast (noun) the first meal you eat in the morning (bữa ăn đầu tiên trong ngày mà bạn ăn vào buổi sáng sớm)
I have eggs for breakfast. (Tôi ăn trứng vào bữa sáng.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

A place where people buy and sell food and other things
questions.explanation:
market (noun) a place where people buy and sell food and other things (nơi mọi người tập trung để mua bán thực phẩm và các hàng hóa khác)
My mother goes to the market every morning. (Mẹ tôi đi chợ mỗi buổi sáng.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

The study of the world and how things work
questions.explanation:
science (noun) the study of the world and how things work (môn học nghiên cứu về thế giới tự nhiên và cách mọi thứ vận hành)
Science is my favourite subject. (Khoa học là môn học yêu thích của tôi.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

Saying no, or being bad and unhappy
questions.explanation:
negative (adjective) saying no, or being bad and unhappy (thể hiện sự phủ nhận, từ chối hoặc cảm xúc tiêu cực và không tốt)
Try not to have a negative feeling. (Hãy cố gắng không có cảm xúc tiêu cực.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

Showing who is meant to get or use something
questions.explanation:
for (preposition) showing who is meant to get or use something (dùng để chỉ ra đối tượng hoặc mục đích mà điều gì đó được dành riêng)
This gift is for you. (Món quà này là dành cho bạn.)

make
questions.explanation: make a mistake = mắc lỗi

Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

single
questions.explanation: single room = phòng đơn

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

go
questions.explanation: go camping = đi cắm trại

Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

give
questions.explanation: give a lecture = giảng bài

Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

do
questions.explanation: do a degree = học lấy bằng

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

I was ___ about the best place to go for a summer holiday.
questions.explanation: wondering = băn khoăn

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

The hotel ___ comfortable accommodation for up to one hundred guests every night.
questions.explanation: provides = cung cấp

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

The 4.05 train to the city has been ___ because of the heavy snow.
questions.explanation: cancelled = hủy

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

Travelling on the underground in the city is fast and very ___.
questions.explanation: convenient = tiện lợi

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

Was the swimming pool very ___ when you arrived there this afternoon?
questions.explanation: crowded = đông đúc

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

I spent the whole evening ___ essays that my students had written last week.
questions.explanation: marking = chấm

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

Scientists know a lot about the mental ___ of young children these days.
questions.explanation: development = phát triển

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

Simon left school early with no ___ and struggled to find a good job.
questions.explanation: qualifications = bằng cấp

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

The police have carried out an ___ search of the whole forest area.
questions.explanation: extensive = trên diện rộng

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

Being a good doctor ___ a lot of skill, patience and years of training.
questions.explanation: demands = đòi hỏi

questions.content:
Writing — Part 3 - Three responses

Why is doing sport / staying active important?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think sport is important because it keeps our bodies strong and healthy. Regular exercise improves our heart and muscles, helps us control our weight, and can prevent illnesses such as diabetes and high blood pressure.

questions.content:
Writing — Part 3 - Three responses

Why is doing sport / staying active important?
questions.sampleAnswer: For me, staying active is also essential for mental health. After a busy day, I go for a run or play badminton. It clears my mind, reduces stress, and usually helps me sleep better at night.

questions.content:
Writing — Part 3 - Three responses

Why is doing sport / staying active important?
questions.sampleAnswer: Team sports have given me more than fitness. When I play football, I meet people with similar interests and learn to communicate, cooperate, and solve problems together. These experiences have helped me make close friends and feel more confident.

questions.content:
Writing — Part 4 - Informal and formal emails

Write an email to your friend Mai. Tell her that you have joined a sports club, describe your experience, and invite her to try it with you. Write 40-50 words.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Hi Mai,

I’ve just joined Riverside Sports Club, and I’m really enjoying it. The trainers are friendly, the gym is modern, and I tried a fun beginner’s badminton session yesterday. Would you like to come with me next Saturday? We can join the free trial class together!

Best,
Linh

questions.content:
Writing — Part 4 - Informal and formal emails

Write an email to the manager of Riverside Sports Club. Suggest an improvement or a new activity/class you would like the club to offer, and explain why it would benefit members. Write 120-150 words.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Dear Manager,

I am writing to suggest that Riverside Sports Club introduce a weekly beginner-friendly yoga and stretching class in the early evening. Although the club offers excellent gym equipment and team sports, many members, including me, would appreciate a calmer activity after work.

This class could focus on improving flexibility, posture, and relaxation, with simple exercises suitable for people of different ages and fitness levels. It would also help members recover safely after more demanding activities, such as football or weight training. Holding it at 6.30 p.m. on weekdays would allow office workers to attend.

In addition, a yoga class may attract new members who are not interested in competitive sports. I believe it would make the club more inclusive and encourage existing members to visit more often.

Yours faithfully,
Linh

Sắp xếp các câu theo thứ tự đúng:

  1. In the early days of cinema, audiences were fascinated by silent, black-and-white films shown in crowded theatres.
  2. Because these films had no recorded dialogue, pianists or small orchestras often played music live to accompany the action on screen.
  3. This changed in the late 1920s, when new technology made it possible for filmmakers to add synchronized speech and sound effects.
  4. As a result, films became more realistic, and colour cinema later gave directors another powerful way to tell stories visually.
  5. More recently, digital cameras, computer-generated images, and advanced editing have allowed studios to create spectacular modern blockbusters.
  6. Meanwhile, audiences no longer need to visit a cinema to see them, since many people now stream movies on televisions, laptops, or phones.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

Can you describe your room? What does it look like, what furniture do you have, and what is your favourite thing in your room?
questions.sampleAnswer: My room is small but bright. The walls are white, and there is a big window near my bed. I have a bed, a desk, a chair, and a wardrobe. My favourite thing is my desk because I study and draw there.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

What activities do you do with your family? When do you do them, and how often?
questions.sampleAnswer: I often cook dinner with my family at weekends. My mother makes soup, and I wash vegetables or set the table. We also watch a film together on Sunday evening. We do these activities once or twice a week because everyone is usually busy.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

What do you usually do with friends in your free time? Where do you go, and why do you enjoy it?
questions.sampleAnswer: In my free time, I usually meet my friends at a café near our school. We talk, drink juice, and sometimes play board games. I like being with them because we laugh a lot and I can forget about homework for a while.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Describe the picture.
questions.sampleAnswer: In this picture, I can see a mother and her young child sitting on a sofa in their living room. They are reading a book together. The mother is sitting next to the child, and she is holding the book open. The child is looking at the pages carefully. Both of them are smiling, so they look very happy and interested in the story. The sofa looks soft and comfortable. I think it is a quiet afternoon or evening at home. They may be reading a story about animals, adventures, or a funny character. I like this picture because the mother and child are spending good time together. Reading with parents can be fun, and it can help children learn new words.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

What do you usually watch on television?
questions.sampleAnswer: I usually watch television in the evening after dinner. I like comedy programmes because they make me laugh and help me relax. I also enjoy cartoons and animal shows. My favourite programme is a cooking show because I can learn easy recipes. At weekends, I sometimes watch a film with my family. However, I do not watch TV for many hours. I prefer reading afterwards.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Do you think reading books or watching television is better for children's learning and imagination?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think reading books is better than watching television for children's learning and imagination. Books help children learn new words and understand stories. When they read, they can make pictures in their heads. This is good for imagination. Television can teach children in animal or science programmes. However, children only look at a screen, so they may not think as much.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Compare these two pictures.
questions.sampleAnswer:
In both pictures, people are having a meeting at work. They are sitting in a room and listening to other people. The meetings look formal and the people may be talking about their jobs or making plans.

However, there are some clear differences. In the first picture, the meeting is very large. There are many people sitting in rows, like at a conference. One person may be speaking at the front, so it is difficult for everyone to talk. The room is also big and busy. In the second picture, there are only four people. They sit around one table and look at each other. This meeting seems quieter and friendlier. Each person can share an idea more easily. I think the small meeting is more active.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Would you prefer a large meeting or a small meeting? Why?
questions.sampleAnswer: I would prefer a small meeting with a few people. First, I feel more comfortable speaking in a small group. I can explain my ideas and ask questions without feeling nervous. Also, it is easier to listen to everyone and understand the main topic. Large meetings can be useful, but they are often noisy and impersonal. A small meeting is better for discussion.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Why are teamwork and meetings important in the modern workplace?
questions.sampleAnswer: Teamwork is very important in the modern workplace because one person cannot do every task alone. People have different skills, so they can help each other and produce better work. Meetings are useful because workers can share news, plan tasks, and talk about problems. A good meeting can save time and stop mistakes. However, meetings should be short and clear, so people return to work.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 4 - Discuss an abstract topic

Talk about a gift you received that was special to you. What was it, who gave it to you, and how did you feel when you received it?
questions.sampleAnswer:
The most special gift I received was a small blue watch. My older sister gave it to me on my eighteenth birthday. It was not expensive, but it was very beautiful and useful. The watch had a simple round face and a soft strap. My sister knew that I was often late for school because I did not wear a watch.

When I opened the box, I felt surprised and very happy. I could see that she had thought carefully about my daily life. She also wrote a short card saying, “I hope this helps you arrive on time.” I laughed when I read it.

I wore the watch every day for a long time. It reminded me of my sister and her kind advice. Now I use my phone to check the time, but I still keep the watch in my room. For me, it is special because it shows her love, not because it costs a lot of money.
